item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
444
ABPZ20 KNHC 070512
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Sun Sep 6 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Lowell, located several hundred miles south-southwest of Lihue,
Hawaii, and on Tropical Storm Marie, located several hundred miles
west-southwest of Punta Eugenia, Mexico. The National Hurricane
Center has issued the last advisory on Post-Tropical Cyclone Karina,
located several hundred miles east-northeast of the Big Island of
Hawaii.

Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of disorganized showers and thunderstorms associated with a
trough of low pressure is located several hundred miles
south-southwest of southwestern Mexico. Gradual development of this
system is possible, and a tropical depression could form during the
middle or latter portions of the week while the system moves
generally west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...50 percent.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Beven

item.title: Tropical Storm Marie Public Advisory Number 25
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Mon Sep 07 2026 
614 
WTPZ33 KNHC 070848
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Marie Advisory Number  25
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
200 AM PDT Mon Sep 07 2026
 
...MARIE EXPECTED TO CONTINUE TO PRODUCE DANGEROUS BEACH CONDITIONS
ALONG THE COAST OF BAJA CALIFORNIA AND SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA
FOR THE NEXT SEVERAL DAYS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM PDT...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...24.4N 123.7W
ABOUT 580 MI...935 KM WSW OF PUNTA EUGENIA MEXICO
ABOUT 700 MI...1125 KM SW OF SAN DIEGO CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...65 MPH...100 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 305 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...986 MB...29.12 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM PDT (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Marie was
located near latitude 24.4 North, longitude 123.7 West. Marie is
moving toward the northwest near 8 mph (13 km/h). A slight turn
toward the west-northwest is forecast to occur soon. Marie is then
expected to resume a northwestward heading at a faster forward speed
by Tuesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 65 mph (100 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Steady weakening is expected to continue for the 
next several days, and Marie is forecast to become a post-tropical 
remnant low Tuesday night or early Wednesday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 115 miles (185 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 986 mb (29.12 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Marie will continue to affect portions of
the coast of the Baja California Peninsula and southern California
for the next couple of days. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office. A depiction of rip current
risk for the United States can be found at:
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Beven

item.title: Tropical Storm Marie Forecast Discussion Number 25
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Mon Sep 07 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 070849
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Marie Discussion Number  25
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
200 AM PDT Mon Sep 07 2026

Marie continues show signs of gradual weakening via satellite 
imagery. Based on the infrared satellite imagery, the convection 
continues to wane and water vapor shows that the dry air continues 
to intrude into the center of the storm. A partial ASCAT pass from 
METOP-C showed that the winds on the western side of the storm are 
limited to about 100 nm and some of the strongest wind speeds were 
around 45 kt. The most recent TAFB Dvorak fix came in at T3.5/55 kt, 
while the UW-CIMSS objective intensity estimates are in the range of 
39-57 kt. Therefore, the initial intensity has been lowered to 55 kt 
for this advisory. 
 
The storm is moving slowly northwestward. A general northwestward
motion with some increase in forward speed is expected over the
next few days as Marie moves into a weakness in the subtropical
ridge toward a mid- to upper-level low. Only minor adjustments have 
been made to the current NHC track forecast compared to the 
previous forecast and aligns with the HCCA and GDMI models. 
 
Steady weakening is expected to continue as Marie moves over 
progressively cooler waters and into an even drier air mass over the 
next few days. In addition, southwesterly vertical wind shear is 
anticipated to notably increase beginning Tuesday. The combination 
of these factors should lead to cyclone degenerating into a remnant 
low, which is still predicted to occur by 60 hours. However, it is 
possible that this could occur sooner as the GFS simulated satellite 
imagery has Marie becoming post-tropical at an earlier time. The 
current NHC intensity forecast is similar to the previous one and is 
in line with most of the model guidance.
 
While Marie is well away from land, large swells from the
storm have been affecting portions of the coast of the Baja
California Peninsula and southern California. These conditions
will likely continue to cause dangerous beach conditions over the
next several days.
